Seven Lies You've Been Told about Work

This is a complicated topic in my opinion. What the article makes clear is that work is not inherently important or necessary. That is to say that there is nothing about work that makes somebody's life better outside of the context of what work can provide financially.

But the inescapable fact is that for the majority of people, work is how they're going to get by, and that will be the case for a very long time, multiple lifetimes at least. We're not exactly due for a fullblown socialist revolution backed up by the technology to make sure everybody is okay, even if the technology exists now and most people could be supported by a benevolent state without much issue. The path there, however, is a different story, as is the will of the general public to want that outcome or even find it desirable. As much as most people hate work, they hate "socialism" more, even if it's a term that causes more negative gut reaction than intellectual understanding in most people.

So while I agree that work isn't all it's cracked up to be, and really not even close, life is pretty shitty when you're behind on rent and don't know how you're going to pay your credit card bill when it comes due. Work is honestly more desirable than poverty. Until we have a system that can support people who don't work without them being a massive burden on society at large, we're just going to have to work.
